title: My Home
description: Name rooms and give a simple description of a home.
objectives: Name rooms and give a simple description of a home.

stages.title: Understand the language
stages.instructions: Read the explanation, examples, common error, and recap.

blocks.text: This lesson prepares you to name rooms and give a simple description of a home. The central language is be, have, and room nouns. It belongs to the practical context of home & around town. Focus first on meaning: decide what information the listener needs. Then choose the subject, verb form, and useful detail. At A1, keep the message short and concrete. One clear sentence is enough before the other person responds. The same language returns in the listening, repeat, speaking, exercises, and guided conversation stages.

blocks.explanation: Use this model to begin the my home exchange.

blocks.english: The kitchen is next to the living room.
blocks.explanation: This my home model adds a different detail or response.
Use this question or response to keep the my home exchange moving.

blocks.text: Notice the two models: “My home has two bedrooms.” and “The kitchen is next to the living room.” They show the pattern in complete communication, not as isolated grammar. Say the model aloud, replace one detail, and check that the new sentence keeps the intended meaning. When the other person asks a follow-up question, answer directly and add a relevant detail. This makes the exchange natural while keeping the language controlled.

blocks.title: Common error
blocks.text: Do not mix the word order or verb form with another pattern. Keep the controlled form for this lesson: be, have, and room nouns.
